title: Sex-specific serum phosphate does not clearly improve cross-survey prediction of elevated CRP beyond routine nonlinear predictors
abstract: We tested whether female×(serum phosphate−3.5mg/dL) improves concurrent CRP>3mg/L classification beyond separate phosphate, sex and routine nonlinear predictors. Weighted models trained in NHANES III (14,403 adults) were transported without tuning to separately recruited NHANES2017–2018 (4,596 adults). Weighted Brier changed from 0.17186023 to 0.17177977: delta -0.00008046, approximate fixed-fit target-PSU95% interval [-0.00036906,0.00021211]; AUC delta 0.00042634. Joint discovery-refit/target intervals also crossed zero. Discovery out-of-fold Brier worsened; food-fast adjustment retained a small point gain and an older-adult sensitivity worsened. An artificial −0.2mg/dL target phosphate shift reversed the point effect. This is an inconclusive incremental-prediction result for one representation, not evidence against sex-dependent phosphate physiology or a clinical diagnostic test.
